title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose:
This page consolidates Redwood Inference sales enablement assets and guidance for prospect-facing motions: positioning & messaging, competitive briefs, pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a security FAQ tailored to prospects. Use these materials for SDR/AE outreach, demo prep, and RFP responses.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Positioning: Redwood is the production-first inference platform that makes LLM inference predictable, economical, and portable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Key differentiators: unified runtime across environments, cost-aware controls (batching, caching, quantization recommendations), and enterprise-grade reliability + rollout tooling.
- Sales assets: canonical pitch deck, battlecards for top competitors, pricing reference, ROI calculator, and security FAQ for prospects.

1) Positioning & Messaging (one-liners + persona hooks)
-- Elevator pitch (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable latency and cost at scale across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—letting teams ship LLM features without owning the serving stack.

-- Value props by persona:
- Engineering / ML Engineer: "Same API, consistent performance everywhere — reduce ops and avoid model-ops fragmentation. Built-in caching, KV-management, and kernel selection mean faster time-to-scale and lower per-token costs."
- Platform / Infra Lead: "Reserve capacity and enforce SLOs with Dedicated pools and autoscaling policies. Centralized observability and rollout tooling simplify operations across teams."
- Security / Compliance: "Private deployments, VPC/on-prem options, KMS/HSM integration, and auditable logs let you meet regulatory requirements without custom infra."
- Product / PM: "Focused on predictable UX — low tail latency, model versioning, and canary rollouts minimize regressions to end users."

-- Messaging pillars (always include):
1. Predictable performance: Latency SLOs (p50/p95 targets), dedicated GPU pools, and smart routing.
2. Production economics: Batching, caching, and quantization advice to lower per-token costs.
3. Unified deployment modes: Host-to-private parity reduces fragmentation & vendor lock-in.
4. Reliability & graceful degradation: Model fallbacks and region routing to keep the app online.

2) Competitive briefs and battlecards
-- Competitive landscape (short):
- General cloud AI platforms (BigCloudAI): managed endpoints + standard infra — strength in scale and breadth, weaker in inference economics and transparent performance guarantees.
- LLM API providers (LLMAPI Co): simple API & model access — strengths: ease-of-use; weaknesses: fewer deployment modes, less control over latency/cost.
- Inference infra vendors (OpenServe Tech): self-hosted runtimes for teams that want full control — strengths: control & cost when fully staffed; weaknesses: engineering burden and slower go-to-market.

-- Battlecard template (use for each competitor):
- Competitor: [name]
- Positioning summary: 1–2 lines
- Strengths: 3 bullets (where they win)
- Weaknesses / customer risks: 3 bullets (where Redwood can win)
- Objection handling: canned responses and evidence (benchmarks, case studies)
- Recommended demo play: which feature to show to win (routing, cost calculator, canary deploy)

-- Example callouts: 
- Against BigCloudAI: emphasize our inference economics (transparent per-token unit costs + batching/quantization guidance) and private deployment parity. Provide a 3rd-party benchmark PDF and p95 latency charts for standard workloads.
- Against LLMAPI Co: emphasize dedicated capacity and enterprise rollout controls; use the enterprise case study (RegTech customer) showing throughput and SLA compliance.

3) Pitch deck outline (canonical deck for AEs)
Use the canonical pitch deck from the shared drive. Core slides (recommended order):
1. Cover + value prop (1 slide)
2. Market problem: challenges of serving LLMs in production (1–2 slides)
3. Redwood solution: runtime + orchestration + deployment parity (2 slides)
4. Differentiators & architecture diagram (1 slide)
5. Performance & cost benchmarks (p50/p95 / tokens/sec / $/1000 tokens) (2 slides)
6. Enterprise features: Dedicated, Private, Security & compliance (1–2 slides)
7. Customer case studies & ROI (2 slides)
8. Pricing overview & commercial motions (1 slide)
9. Roadmap & partnership options (1 slide)
10. Next steps / pilot proposal (1 slide)

Deck tips: open with a concise ROI statement; bring a one-page technical appendix for SREs; always include a demo link and ask for workload metrics to tailor the pilot.

4) Pricing guidance (reference for AEs)
-- Pricing tiers (high level, use as guidance only — check deals desk for exceptions):
- Hosted (self-serve): usage-based pricing; token-based tiers with volume discounts. Example bucket: $0.003 / 1k tokens (base) with sliding discounts at >100M tokens/month.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed spend with configurable GPU pool sizes and SLAs. Typical starting commit: $50k/month for small Dedicated pool (example). Includes baseline throughput & prescriptive autoscaling policy.
- Private (enterprise licensing): platform fee + services (on-prem/air-gapped packaging, KMS/HSM integrations). Multi-year license + optional support tiers.

-- Pricing play guidance:
- Early-stage / volume sellers: offer Hosted pilot + 30-day technical support and a 90-day ROI lookback.
- Enterprise customers: propose a 6–12 month Dedicated trial with phased commit and a rollback clause.
- For regulated customers: combine Private licensing with dedicated onboarding & compliance validation (add-on).

-- Discount guardrails: consult Deals Desk. Never promise more than two quarters of free Dedicated capacity without product approval. All exceptions require legal & finance sign-off.

5) Representative case studies (templates & short abstracts)
-- Case Study: Converso (AI-native startup)
Problem: Converso needed sub-250ms p95 latency for a conversational UX while keeping inference cost under $0.50 per active user/month.
Solution: Hosted API + prefix caching + model quantization recommendations; tuned batching.
Result: Reduced median latency from 520ms to 180ms, p95 to 240ms, and inference cost per user down 45% versus prior hosted provider.

-- Case Study: RegTech Inc. (enterprise, private deployment)
Problem: Highly regulated customer required on-prem inference with auditable keys and monthly retention policies.
Solution: Private deployment with KMS/HSM integration, dedicated observability, and SSO + RBAC.
Result: Successful SOC 2 readiness review, 99.95% uptime in the first 6 months, and a 3x speedup in model iteration time for their compliance workflows.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (top questions & canonical answers)
Q: What compliance frameworks do you support?
A: Redwood supports SOC 2 Type II (in hosted and Dedicated contexts), and provides compliance packages and evidence for enterprise customers pursuing ISO 27001 and regional data residency. For Private deployments we provide documentation and integrations to assist in customer audits.

Q: How is customer data isolated and encrypted?
A: Data-in-transit is TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3; at-rest encryption uses AES-256. Customers can bring keys via KMS or HSM for Private and Dedicated deployments. Access to logs and audit trails is role-based and can be exported to customer SIEM.

Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. Private deployment options include a customer-managed control plane (VPC peering) and a packaged on-prem installer for air-gapped environments. Professional services help validate networking and upgrade procedures.

Q: Where does customer data persist and how long is it retained?
A: By default, ephemeral inference logs are retained for 30 days in Hosted. Dedicated and Private customers can configure retention policies; enterprise retention & residency options available per contract.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and access controls?
A: Yes. We provide audit logging, RBAC, SSO/SAML, and integration hooks for SIEMs. Logs include request metadata, model version, and response status for traceability.

Q: What are your SLAs and reliability guarantees?
A: Dedicated customers receive SLA-backed uptime commitments (example: 99.9% monthly uptime). Hosted customers have published SLO targets and incident response processes; details available on the legal SLA page (link in related pages).

Q: How do you prevent model/regression quality issues during rollouts?
A: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B testing, automated fallback to compatible model variants, and integrated evals tied to prompt sets to detect quality regressions before they reach end users.

7) Sales plays and objection handling (common objections with counters)
-- Objection: "We can self-host; why pay?"
Counter: "OpenServe-style self-hosting gives control but requires heavy engineering + maintenance. Redwood reduces time-to-value, offers production optimizations (kernel selection, KV cache, batching), and a single support contract for runtime + orchestration."

-- Objection: "We need strict data residency and a totally air-gapped solution."
Counter: "We offer Private deployments with on-prem packaging and professional services to validate air-gapped installs. Provide the RegTech case study as proof point."

-- Objection: "We care most about inference cost."
Counter: "Walk through our Optimize recommendations, batching and quantization profiles, and show a tailored ROI estimate using their token profile. Provide prior client outcomes (e.g., 40–60% cost savings in comparable workloads)."

9) Process for requesting custom collateral or approved exceptions
1. Fill the collateral request form (link in shared drive) with target persona, requested assets, and timeline.
2. Go-to-market team reviews within 3 business days.
3. For pricing exceptions or custom legal terms, route to Deals Desk and Legal; expect 5–10 business days for standard reviews.

Appendix: Approved claims and evidence
- Approved latency claims: p50 and p95 numbers must reference specific benchmark (include workload name & model). Do not generalize without referencing the canonical benchmark doc.
- Pricing claims: only discuss public list prices and approved discount ranges. All bespoke pricing requires Deals Desk review.
